what_text: The specified value is the figure decided in advance for how this part is tightened in this process.
where_text: It is in the tightening condition column of the work order or on the drawing for that part.
question_examples: What is a specified value?||What do you mean by the specified value?

what_text: The process standard is the document the factory has agreed that sets out the method and conditions for that process.
where_text: It is in the procedure folder at the workstation or in the production shared folder.
question_examples: What is the process standard?||Where is the process standard?

what_text: The work order is the sheet or tablet display that tells you what is being built here today and how.
where_text: It is in the holder at the bench or on the job screen of the terminal.
question_examples: Which one is the work order?||Where is the work order?

what_text: The nominal diameter is the figure for the thickness of the screw. It is the number after the letter M.
where_text: It is on the label of the box the screws came in or in the parts column of the work order.
question_examples: What is the nominal diameter?||Which dimension is the nominal diameter?

what_text: The pitch is the spacing between neighbouring threads. Two screws of the same thickness will not mate if this spacing differs.
where_text: It is on the box label or on the drawing for the part.
question_examples: What is pitch?||I do not follow what pitch means.

what_text: A coarse thread is the ordinary pitch that is set as standard for that thickness.
where_text: If the box marking carries no pitch figure it is normally coarse.
question_examples: What does coarse mean?||What does it mean when it says coarse?

what_text: A fine thread has the same thickness but the threads are spaced more closely than a coarse thread.
where_text: On the box marking a pitch figure after the M number means it is fine.
question_examples: What is a fine thread?||How do I tell a fine thread?

aliases: designation||the marking on the screw||the code
what_text: The thread designation is the letter M with numbers that gives the thickness and the pitch.
where_text: It is on the box label or in the parts column of the work order.
question_examples: What is the thread designation?||Which bit is the thread designation?

what_text: The part number is the alphanumeric code assigned to that one kind of screw.
where_text: It is on the label of the box the screws came in or in the parts column of the work order.
question_examples: What is a part number?||Where is the part number written?

aliases: grade||strength class||how strong the bolt is
what_text: The strength grade is the class that tells you how much load that bolt will take.
where_text: It is stamped on the face of the bolt head as numbers separated by a dot.
question_examples: What is the strength grade?||Where do I look for the strength grade?

what_text: The head marking is the numbers or symbols stamped on the head of the bolt.
where_text: Look down at the head of the bolt and you will see the raised characters on the face.
question_examples: What is a head marking?||Where is the head marking?

what_text: The tightening torque is how much turning force you apply to the screw. It is measured in newton meters.
where_text: It is in the tightening condition column of the work order or on the drawing for the part.
question_examples: What is tightening torque?||I do not know what torque means.

aliases: axial force||the force pulling the parts together
what_text: The clamp load is the force with which the tightened screw pulls the parts together. It results from the torque you apply.
where_text: You cannot see the clamp load directly. It is controlled through the torque set in the process standard.
question_examples: What is clamp load?||Where do I measure clamp load?

what_text: Lubrication means whether there is oil or grease on the screw and on the faces being clamped.
where_text: Look at the surface of the screw and judge whether it is wet and shiny or dry.
question_examples: What does lubrication mean?||How do I judge the lubrication?

aliases: what you screw into||the part being clamped||base material
what_text: The mating material is the part the screw is driven into and what that part is made of.
where_text: It is the part you are about to fasten. The material is on the drawing or the parts list.
question_examples: What is the mating material?||Which one is the mating material?

what_text: A washer is the thin ring that goes between the head of the screw and the part.
where_text: Look under the head of the screw and you can see whether a ring is fitted.
question_examples: What is a washer?||Which part is the washer?

what_text: A pilot hole is the hole drilled before the screw goes in. The thread is either formed in it or cut with a tap.
where_text: The diameter is in the hole note on the drawing or in the machining standard table.
question_examples: What is a pilot hole?||Where is the pilot hole size written?

aliases: female thread||the thread inside the hole
what_text: A tapped hole is the thread cut on the inside of a hole. It mates with the thread on the bolt.
where_text: Look into the hole in the part and you can see the spiral ridges.
question_examples: What is a tapped hole?||Where is the tapped hole?

what_text: A tapping screw forms its own thread as it drives into a pilot hole. The tip is narrow and pointed.
where_text: Look at the tip of the screw. If it is pointed it is a tapping screw.
question_examples: What is a tapping screw?||How do I tell a tapping screw?

what_text: A machine screw goes into a hole or nut that is already threaded. Its tip is flat.
where_text: Look at the tip of the screw. If it is cut off flat it is a machine screw.
question_examples: What is a machine screw?||How is that different from a machine screw?

what_text: Galling is when the screw and the mating metal rub and effectively weld together so the screw stops turning.
where_text: If it suddenly goes stiff and stops moving partway in, suspect galling.
question_examples: What is galling?||What sort of state is galling?

what_text: The pull out strength is how much force the tightened screw will take before it pulls out of the mating material.
where_text: It is set by the pilot hole diameter and how deep the thread engages. Check the machining standard.
question_examples: What is pull out strength?||Strength against what?

aliases: reuse rule||criteria for using it again
what_text: The reuse criteria are the factory rule for whether a screw that has been removed may be fitted again.
where_text: It is inside the process standard or in the notes on the drawing for that part.
question_examples: What are the reuse criteria?||Where do I find the reuse criteria?

what_text: The plate thickness is the thickness of the plate the screw is driven into.
where_text: It is the section dimension on the drawing or in the material column of the work order.
question_examples: What is plate thickness?||Which dimension is the plate thickness?

what_text: The process is the label for which line and which piece of equipment this work happens on.
where_text: It is on the plate attached to the machine or at the top of the work order.
question_examples: What do you mean by process?||Where is the process name written?

aliases: head shape||shape of the head||where the tool goes
what_text: The drive type is the shape of the part you put the tool into. It can be a hex socket, an external hex, a cross and so on.
where_text: Look down at the head of the screw and you can tell from the socket shape or the outer shape.
question_examples: What is the drive type?||Which part is the head shape?

what_text: The screw type is the division by how it is used, such as a machine screw or a tapping screw.
where_text: You can tell from the shape of the tip and from the product name on the box label.
question_examples: What do you mean by screw type?||What should I say for the type?

aliases: what is happening||the state it is in
what_text: The symptom is what is actually happening to the screw right now.
where_text: Turn the screw in your hand and describe how it moves.
question_examples: What do you mean by symptom?||What should I tell you about the symptom?
